chunks: What Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā narrated from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, from ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd, from Muṣaddiq ibn Ṣadaqah, from ʿAmmār ibn Mūsā, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a man who goes out for some need and travels five farsakhs or six farsakhs, then comes to a village and stays there, then departs from it and travels five farsakhs or six farsakhs—this does not qualify—and then he stays in that place.

He said: He is not considered a traveler until he travels eight farsakhs from his home or village, so he should perform the salat in full. For this narration is restricted to one who left his home without the intention of travel, then the journey continues with him until he becomes a traveler without intent; in that case, completing the salat is incumbent upon him. Even if the distance exceeds that for which, had he intended it, shortening would have been obligatory upon him, completion is only binding on him because he did not intend a journey whose amount reaches that in which shortening becomes obligatory. And that which supports this interpretation is...

key_terms.ثَمَانِيَةَ فَرَاسِخَ: eight farsakhs, the legal distance threshold mentioned for travel
key_terms.فَلْيُتِمَّ الصَّلَاةَ: he should complete the salat (prayer) in full rather than shorten it
key_terms.مَقْصُورَةٌ: restricted or limited in application to a particular case
key_terms.مُسَافِرًا: a legally recognized traveler for whom travel rulings apply
key_terms.نِيَّةِ السَّفَرِ: the intention to undertake travel, which affects the ruling

ai.seo_question: When does a person become a traveler required to shorten salat (prayer) according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the legal measure of travel for the purpose of shortening salat (prayer). It indicates that a person is not treated as a traveler unless the journey from his original home or village reaches eight farsakhs, and it further distinguishes between intended travel and a distance that accumulates without an initial intention of travel.
